claim: Rev A's 40 to 80 fibres (0.011 to 0.022 m2) cannot give 200 mL/min at 10 kPa with any listed grade; filling the bore with about 220 fibres raises the area 2.5 times
law: Darcy flux J = Lp x TMP over the outer fibre area; SepraPor minima at 25 C converted to 20 C
check: 80 fibres x 110 mm: 46 mL/min (0.1 um) to 78 mL/min (0.2 um); 40 x 90 mm: 19 mL/min. Fixed by a full-bore bundle (0.056 m2, packing 48%, no central tube); the fix is necessary, not sufficient: the flow target then rests on the grade (S2, S3)

claim: Full-bore bundle with a 0.2 um MF fibre gives at least the 150 mL/min of PR-002 (HWA-DEC-001 D3) at 10 kPa, clean water, 20 C, straw upright
law: Stage sum: lift, intake, membrane, lumen and potting (Hagen-Poiseuille), grids, carbon (Ergun), pad (Darcy), mouth
check: 179 mL/min at 10 kPa; 200 mL/min needs 11.0 kPa, or Lp 3,419 L/(m2 h bar) at 20 C, above the grade's listed minimum (2,930). Dipped to the dip line and primed: 191; 245 mm body: 213. Against the decided 150 mL/min upper-bound target the 0.2 um grade has about 19 % margin; uncertainties (pad, carbon, area basis) run mostly downward (independent review 2026-11-11), so TC confirms it
closed_by: Fix: target set to 150 mL/min, HWA-DEC-001 D3 (Amish, 2026-11-11); test TC at TRL 4

claim: The 0.1 um MF fibre gives less than the 150 mL/min target and is used only if the 0.2 um grade fails the retention criteria of HWA-DEC-001 D2
law: Same stage sum
check: 110 mL/min at 10 kPa; 200 mL/min needs 17.1 kPa. The shortfall is accepted only as the safety trade-off D2 defines (thin bacteria); the 245 mm body is the TRL 4 revision if trials need it
closed_by: Fix: grade selection rule HWA-DEC-001 D2 and target D3 (Amish, 2026-11-11)

claim: A true ultrafiltration fibre (100 kDa) cannot give usable flow at suction in this envelope, so the membrane must be a microfiltration grade
law: SepraPor UF 100 kDa 215 to 550 L/(m2 h bar) at 25 C
check: 15 to 37 mL/min at 10 kPa. Fixed: PR-004 floor 1,800 L/(m2 h bar) at 25 C (1,600 at 20 C), the floor for usable flow (110 mL/min); PR-002 itself needs 3,419 at 20 C, which no listed grade guarantees (S2)

claim: The 400 mL/min that straw users want is not reachable at a comfortable 10 kPa sip, so it is not a requirement; PR-002 states 150 mL/min as an upper bound
law: Stage sum; 400 mL/min threshold from the concept validation questions
check: 110 to 179 mL/min, under half; 400 mL/min needs 21 to 33 kPa. Not reachable in this envelope; stated to users as a known limit

claim: A child at 5 kPa draws 45 to 74 mL/min and an elderly user at 7 kPa 71 to 116 mL/min; 1.5 L takes a child 20 to 33 min of sipping
law: Persona suction assumed 5 and 7 kPa (STANDARDS 25.6 range 5 to 15 kPa); sustained sip suction of children and older adults is to assess (Wertsen and Stenberg 2017 measured adult lip force only)
check: Stage sum; at 5 C the child needs 31 to 50 min per 1.5 L; tilting to 50 mm lift gives 58 to 96 mL/min; fatigue and lip seal on the 10 mm tip to test (TH)

claim: At 200 mL/min the carbon bed costs about 1 kPa of suction
law: Ergun, 12 x 40 GAC, sphericity 0.75, voidage 0.42 (assumed); range 0.5 to 2.0 kPa for 0.6 to 0.84 mm and voidage 0.38 to 0.45
check: claimed 1 kPa, estimate 0.689 kPa (ratio 1.45)
closed_by: HWA-CAL-001 section 4 (membrane 7.3, lift 1.5, pad 0.9, lumen 0.6 kPa)

claim: Lumen and potting pressure drop is small beside the membrane (single open end, 0.5 mm lumen, 102 mm active, 10 mm potting)
law: Hagen-Poiseuille with flow rising along the fibre, full flow through the potting
check: 0.604 kPa <= 1 kPa

claim: Upright with a shallow dip (water surface at 50 mm) the 155 mm lift to the mouth costs 1.5 kPa; at the dip line 0.9 kPa
law: Hydrostatics rho g h; the flow cases assume a primed shell (S28)
check: 1.52 kPa <= 1.6 kPa

claim: Water at 5 C flows about a third slower than at 20 C
law: Viscosity 1.52 against 1.00 mPa s; flux falls as 1/viscosity, lift does not
check: claimed 0.66 ratio, estimate 0.667 ratio (ratio 0.99)

claim: A microfiltration fibre with a supplier-validated absolute rating is designed to retain most bacteria and protozoan cysts; removal is claimed only from laboratory log reductions, and thin bacteria such as Leptospira are not claimed
law: Size exclusion; STANDARDS 25.6 organism sizes; bacterial retention challenge with Brevundimonas diminuta (0.3 to 0.4 um, ASTM F838 method); Leptospira about 0.1 um across passes 0.2 um membranes (Standard Methods 9260 I)
check: Most bacteria 0.5 to 5 um, cysts 3 to 15 um; but the smallest relevant bacteria are 0.1 to 0.4 um, below a 0.2 um nominal label. Fixed: PR-001 asks for an absolute rating with a B. diminuta challenge report; Leptospira added to the exclusions unless tested (TA, TB)

claim: Viruses (0.02 to 0.3 um) are not reliably retained, so no virus claim is made and the product says so
law: Size exclusion; HWP-CLM-001
check: Enteric viruses 0.027 to 0.09 um, below the 0.1 to 0.2 um rating

claim: The 250 um mesh stops grit and debris only, not silt, microbes or chemicals
law: Sieving; Rev A item 2
check: Silt 2 to 63 um and clay under 2 um pass a 250 um aperture; the membrane is the fouling point (S27)

claim: Clean-water flows are upper bounds: turbid water builds a cake on the fibres and the flow falls between backflushes
law: Cake filtration R = Rm + alpha m / A; design flux 213 L/(m2 h) against tens of L/(m2 h) sustained in surface-water plants; 50 mg/L solids, alpha 1e13 to 1e14 m/kg (assumed A13)
check: 0.2 um at 10 kPa after 1, 5 and 20 L: 169, 140, 85 to 116, 48, 15 mL/min. Settle or cloth-strain cloudy water; backflush interval in litres from TE

claim: Once primed, the dirty shell stays full of water while the intake is under water; air trapped in it cuts the working membrane area
law: The shell is closed at the top by the potting and wetted fibres hold air to their bubble point, so trapped air sits above the outside water level (hydrostatics; Young-Laplace)
check: At the dip line, primed 117 to 191 mL/min; with the shell drained above the outside level (71% wetted) 86 to 144; shallow dip unprimed 15 to 26. Dry fibres prime on first use; between uses the intake cover keeps the shell full; a re-prime method or vent to test (TC, D10). Degassing under suction may add bubbles

claim: The 16 x 20 mm carbon bed holds about 2 g, not 5 g
law: Bed volume 4.0 mL x apparent density 0.48 to 0.50 g/mL (12 x 40 coconut GAC sheet)
check: claimed 2 g, estimate 1.93 g (ratio 1.04)

claim: With an empty-bed contact time of 1.2 s at 200 mL/min the carbon is intended to reduce free chlorine taste only
law: Chlorine reduction on GAC is fast; straws with a few grams of carbon are sold as NSF/ANSI 42 for chlorine (retailer listing, not verified against the NSF database); organics and odours need minutes
check: EBCT 0.6 to 2.4 s across 100 to 400 mL/min at about 60 m/h superficial velocity through a 20 mm bed, fast and shallow even for dechlorination; claim limited to chlorine taste, measured under NSF/ANSI 42 before any claim

claim: Carbon life is set by a measured breakthrough curve, not assumed
law: Rev A section 07 (carbon life)
check: Replacement interval to be set from HWP-VER-001 TG; 500 L is a planning assumption only

claim: The straw does no disinfection; with a chlorine co-treatment the contact time is completed in the container before sipping, and the carbon then removes the residual
law: Free chlorine passes MF membranes; GAC removes it in about a second (S15); CT needs minutes (HWP-CLM-001)
check: EBCT 1.2 s against a contact time of 30 min; instruction: dose, wait, then drink through the straw; the membrane's free-chlorine tolerance (ppm h) to confirm (C2)

claim: AS568-018 O-rings (18.77 x 1.78 mm) in male glands with a 19.3 mm floor seal a 22.0 mm bore
law: Static radial gland practice: squeeze 15 to 30 %, stretch under 5 %, fill under 85 %
check: Nominal squeeze 24%, stretch 2.8%, fill 77%, radial gap 0.10 mm. Tolerance stack as printed (+-0.1 mm) 15% to 33%, outside the range; fixed: bores and gland floors reamed or turned to +-0.05 mm, 18% to 30%. The Rev A 20 x 2 mm ring (outside 24 mm) cannot enter a 22 mm bore

claim: Backflush water enters the clean header and leaves through the fibre walls and the intake without passing the carbon
law: Continuity: with the mouthpiece cap plugging the 5 mm bore the carbon branch is dead-ended
check: Socket on the header at 153 mm, below the carbon cartridge; the cap plug must be fitted first (instruction and pictogram); with the cap off the flush runs out of the mouthpiece instead and the fibres are not cleaned

claim: A 20 mL syringe at 50 kPa backflushes at about 556 to 741 mL/min with a 16 N thumb force
law: Membrane resistance in reverse plus the luer tip and 2 mm passage (1.5 velocity heads each); force = pressure x plunger area (20 mm bore, assumed)
check: 20 mL in about 1.6 to 2.2 s; 20 mL is about 0.35 L/m2, so the number of strokes is set in TE; the syringe is filled with water already treated, never from the source (F11)

claim: A firm push on the syringe stays within the membrane's reverse-pressure rating
law: Pressure = force / plunger area; SepraPor lists a maximum TMP of 1.0 bar (0.2 um) and 1.4 bar (0.1 um) and gives no backflush rating
check: 60 N on a 20 mm plunger gives 191 kPa static, about twice the 0.2 um rating; the module's reverse rating is to confirm (C2) and a pressure limit is set by D11

claim: A plunger-hold air check through the backflush socket shows a broken fibre or a failed collar seal (gross defects only)
law: Young-Laplace: a wetted 0.2 um pore holds air to hundreds of kPa; an open 0.5 mm lumen passes air above 0.6 kPa; isothermal compression of the syringe, header and lumen gas
check: The water in the lumens (4.8 mL) and header (2.3 mL) leaves first, so 51 kPa is reached at the 6 mL mark (fix F7, not 13.3 mL); it opens defects of 5.6 um and larger, not bacterial-size ones; pass is a plunger that holds; bubbles show only inverted; dry spots give a false fail; re-prime after (TA, TF)

claim: With the socket plug out and the socket under water, dirty water bypasses the membrane at more than the filtered flow, and the user cannot tell
law: Orifice flow through the 2 mm socket passage at 10 kPa
check: About 506 mL/min, 2.8 to 4.6 times the membrane flow; controls: socket 43 mm above the dip line, tethered plug, dip-line pictogram; a self-closing socket proposed (D12)

claim: Freezing when wet can crack fibres and potting without changing flow, so the straw is not freeze tolerant and says so
law: Water expands about 9 % on freezing
check: No freeze claim; on-product warning; a straw that may have frozen is replaced, since the air check finds gross defects only (S20)

claim: Bacteria can grow on the carbon and in the clean header during wet storage and reach the user directly, since the carbon sits after the barrier and removes any chlorine residual
law: Heterotrophic growth on GAC is well known; Rev A section 05
check: Design: drainable, capped, carbon replaced by volume; saliva and blow-back reach the carbon from the mouth side (D9); regrowth after wet storage to measure (TG)

claim: Every wetted material, the membrane and potting included, is available in a grade listed for drinking-water contact
law: NSF/ANSI/CAN 61 (extraction); 372 for lead in metal parts only (HWP-REG-001 W7)
check: PP, EPDM, silicone, 316L and GAC grades exist; the membrane (PES or PVDF with PVP and a glycerine wetting agent, residual solvent) and the potting (polyurethane or epoxy) need the module maker's listing; a first-flush volume before first use (F11); printed prototypes see known potable test water only and nobody drinks from them

claim: The carbon fines pad wets and passes water at the sip pressure
law: Young-Laplace water entry pressure 4 gamma cos(theta) / d for a 20 um pore
check: Untreated non-woven PP (contact angle about 100 deg) needs about 2.5 kPa to wet, a quarter of the sip; fixed: hydrophilic-treated pad (F6); its permeability is still assumed (C6)

claim: The straw is under 25 cm long and 3 cm across (kit compatible)
law: Concept validation questions, item 39
check: 29.6 mm across <= 30 mm across
closed_by: HWA-CAL-001 section 9 (length 205 mm; 0.4 mm margin across the plug)

claim: The straw weighs under 100 g dry
law: Model volumes x densities (cad_parts.MATERIALS)
closed_by: HWA-CAL-001 section 9 (full of water about 107 g)

claim: About 220 fibres of 0.8 mm fill a 17.2 mm bundle at about 48 % packing
law: Fibre count = packing x (bundle / fibre diameter)^2
check: claimed 220 fibres, estimate 222 fibres (ratio 0.99)
